newsitem.title: PANAMA: Hutchison Whampoa to upgrade Panama ports.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison Whampoa to upgrade Panama ports.

text.p: Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd will begin Saturday a major upgrade of Panama's two largest ports to try and turn them into a regional hub, company officials said.

The company plans to invest more than $50 million in the next five years to increase the number of cargo containers moved each year at Cristobal port on the Atlantic coast and Balboa port on the Pacific, said James Tsien, director of Panama Ports Co, the Panamanian unit of the Hong Kong group.
Hutchison Whampoa won a 25-year concession last year to operate the ports, located at the Panama Canal's points of entry, after making a $22.2 million offer.

Tsien told a news conference the number of cargo containers moved at Cristobal was expected to rise to 294,000 per year from 200,000 and at Balboa to 268,000 from 10,000 by the beginning of next century.

This would make Panama the Hong Kong group's most important and strategic port of the 15 it operates worldwide, said John Meredith, group managing director of Hutchison Port Holdings (HPH), the consortium's port operations unit and the world's largest independent port operator.
"Already in Hong Kong we're getting shipping companies asking when will it be ready so we can start servicing Balboa as a hub port for North and South America," he said.
Company officials said they have reduced the workforce from about 1,500 to some 400. The United States turned over the ports to Panama in 1977 in accordance with bilateral treaties.
